title.value: Population Genomics Approaches for Genetic Characterization of SARS-CoV-2 Lineages
title.justification: The title directly reflects the core focus of the paper, which is on genomic approaches applied to SARS-CoV-2.
title.quote: Mostefai F, Gamache I, N’Guessan A, et al. (2022) Population Genomics Approaches for Genetic Characterization of SARS-CoV-2 Lineages. Front. Med. 9:826746.

extractions.description: The paper discusses the development and application of population genomic tools for the analysis of the genetic diversity of SARS-CoV-2 lineages. It presents a computational framework for real-time genomic surveillance and lineage identification using a large dataset of SARS-CoV-2 sequences. Techniques such as haplotype networks, principal component analysis, and derived allele frequency trajectories are utilized to understand the evolutionary dynamics of the virus during the COVID-19 pandemic's first year. The study highlights the importance of these tools in tracing transmission pathways and designing preventive strategies, albeit without direct focus on climate change themes.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is the genetic characterization of SARS-CoV-2 lineages and their evolution during the pandemic, which is unrelated to climate change.
climate_change_is_central.quote: We present here a set of genomic surveillance tools from population genetics which can be used to better understand the evolution of this virus in humans.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address any climate change issues directly, instead focusing entirely on genomics of a virus related to a global pandemic.
primary_category.quote: To assist in tracing infection pathways and design preventive strategies, a deep understanding of the viral genetic diversity landscape is needed.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes related to climate change in the paper, as it is focused on a virus genetic characterization.
secondary_categories.quote: We demonstrate that, compared to standard phylogenetic approaches, haplotype networks can be computed efficiently on much larger datasets.

primary_sub_category.justification: The focus of the paper does not align with any sub-categories in climate change as it solely addresses SARS-CoV-2.
primary_sub_category.quote: The computational framework presented here is simple to implement and insightful for real-time genomic surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 and could be applied to any pathogen that threatens the health of populations of humans and other organisms.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not involve any secondary climate-related sub-categories, concentrating only on SARS-CoV-2 genomics.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Tajima’s D, a classical population genetics approach, can also be used to investigate SARS-CoV-2 lineage expansions.

applications.justification: This paper does not focus on climate change applications.

new_primary_category.quote: The genome of the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the pathogen that causes coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), has been sequenced at an unprecedented scale leading to a tremendous amount of viral genome sequencing data.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no sub-category relevant to the content of the paper in terms of climate change.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: The study focuses on the computational analysis of SARS-CoV-2.
